title: Split-field PHI pattern not intercepted by telemetry detector
description: During the initial canary interception test run on 2026-09-19, the detector failed to intercept a synthetic SSN pattern split across two JSON fields (field_a: SSN:000, field_b: -00-0000). Six of seven canary patterns passed. The split-field edge case was not covered by the mock detection logic, producing a false negative rate of 0.1429 and blocking the initial deployment.
root_cause: The HermesMock.detect() method checked for the Base64-encoded SSN pattern but did not include logic to detect SSN fragments split across separate JSON fields. The split-field edge case was specified in EDGE_CASE_PATTERNS but not handled in the detection logic.

remediation_steps.action: Identify the failing pattern from the canary results in the evidence receipt
Add split-field detection logic to HermesMock.detect() — check for SSN:000 and -00-0000 appearing together in the serialized payload
Rerun the full canary interception test suite to confirm all 7 patterns pass
Confirm the new passing evidence receipt is saved and hash-chained to the prior fail receipt
Update detector version from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 and commit with change log entry

compensating_controls: Deployment was blocked immediately on fail result — no telemetry was transmitted during the gap period
Fail-closed gateway configuration remained active throughout — unauthorized destinations were unreachable
Evidence receipt chain preserved the original fail receipt for audit history

chain_integrity.notes: The passing receipt references the prior hash of the fail receipt confirming an unbroken evidence chain from failure through remediation to verified closure.

lessons_learned: Split-field and multi-field identifier patterns must be explicitly specified and tested in the detector edge case suite before initial release. The EDGE_CASE_PATTERNS list should drive detection logic implementation — not only test coverage.
recurrence_prevention: Added split-field detection as a required edge case category in the detector specification. All future identifier categories added to EDGE_CASE_PATTERNS must have corresponding detection logic verified before the pattern is added to the test suite.

framework_impact.HIPAA: Temporary gap in technical safeguard coverage for split-field PHI patterns — mitigated by fail-closed gateway and immediate deployment block
framework_impact.SOC2: Temporary gap in CC6.7 transmission restriction for split-field patterns — same mitigation
framework_impact.ISO27001: Temporary gap in A.8.12 DLP coverage for split-field patterns — same mitigation
framework_impact.NIST-CSF: Temporary gap in PR.DS-2 in-transit protection for split-field patterns — same mitigation
